summary: Michael Weiers (1937–2025) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn, where he served as professor from 1972 to 2003, and was an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University around 1993.

Michael Wenger (born 1947) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an M.A. at The New School and studied under Sojun Mel Weitsman. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

Michael Willis is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at the University of Victoria under Siri Gunasinghe and Alan Gowans, and earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Pramod Chandra, later curating at the British Museum.

Michael Witzel (born 1943) is an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Karl Hoffmann, Paul Thieme, Hanns-Peter Schmidt, Johanna Narten, F. B. J. Kuiper, and Jununath Pandit. He held Chairs of Sanskrit at Leiden University and Harvard University.

Michael Zimmermann (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hamburg and studied at Soka University and IRIAB under Lambert Schmithausen and others. He held posts at Stanford and the University of Hamburg.

Michael von Brück (born 1949) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After earning his Promotion at the University of Rostock, he held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (around 1991–2014).

Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and also studied under Jigme Namgyal and Rechungpa.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She completed her PhD at the University of Munich and was an exchange student at Komazawa University. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and became Assistant Professor at Stanford University.

Michaël Peyrot is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University from 1999 to 2010 and held posts there as well as at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Bréal (1832–1915) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He served as a professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at the EPHE.

Michel Clasquin-Johnson (born 1960) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his undergraduate and graduate education, including his doctoral thesis, at the University of South Africa, where he held a post beginning in 1990.

Michel Hulin (1936–2026) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and completed his studies at Paris-Sorbonne University under Olivier Lacombe, where he later held a post from 1981 to 1998.

Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h (1943–2014) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from around 1993 to 2008.

Michel Lejeune (1907–2000) was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Meillet. His academic career included posts at the University of Poitiers, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Paris.

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at the University of Geneva, Hanazono University, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Michel Soymié (1924–2002) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS, EFEO, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and was Chair of History and Philosophy of Mediaeval China at the EPHE (1966–1992).

Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Paris Diderot University, studying under Maxime Kaltenmark, Kristofer Schipper, and others. He held academic posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Bordeaux.

Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck. She was a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge, where she worked with postdoctoral mentor Hildegard Diemberger from 2013 to 2015.

Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and was a professor at the University of Naples Federico II.
Michele Martin (born 1942) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her studies at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.
